question.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-3,1,4)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $(r-⟨3,-2,1⟩)\cdot ⟨-2,4,-4⟩=0.$
question.worked_solution:
Let's pick a point on the plane, for instance, $Q(3,-2,1).$ Then 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨3,-2,1⟩-⟨-3,1,4⟩ \\  & =⟨6,-3,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, from the equation of the plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨-2,4,-4⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|6\cdot (-2)+(-3)\cdot 4+(-3)\cdot (-4)|}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{4}^{2}+(-4)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-12|}{\sqrt{4+16+16}} \\  & =\frac{|-12|}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
